description: 200 messages of 100 tokens, and no cache breakpoint at all (OpenAI-style traffic). Turn 0 caches 20,000 tokens. Turn 1 adds a message of 400 tokens and the operator cuts it to 100. With no breakpoint the library must search the whole body for the end of the cached prefix: every position is a candidate. The provider read 20,000 tokens, the whole previous body, so B* is the last old message. The new message is past B*, so its 300 saved tokens are fresh input (no breakpoint, so no cache write tier): 300 x $3.00 = +$0.0009. Before the fix the search was quadratic in the number of positions; the result is the same.
